cohort: The study included 392 patients with mild-to-moderate bleeding disorders (MBDs), including 62.8% with bleeding disorder of unknown cause (BDUC), from the Vienna Bleeding Biobank.
finding: Patients with mild-to-moderate bleeding disorders (MBD) have a high risk for recurrent bleeding, with a high bleeding score, blood group O, previous postsurgical bleeding, and an established diagnosis being independent risk factors for various bleeding events.
